Definition: properly, to bend or stoop in kindness to an inferior; to favor, bestow; causatively to implore (i.e. move to favor by petition)
BiblicalUsage: Chanan is bending down in kindness to someone below you, and it is the verb behind grace itself. God tells Moses He will be gracious to whom He will be gracious, Jacob tells Esau the children are the ones God has graciously given him, Solomon prays that God will hear His people when they turn and make supplication, and the blessing on Israel asks the LORD to be gracious unto thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the verb the whole gospel stands on: God stoops. He does not wait for us to climb to Him; He bends down in kindness to the inferior, and that is grace. I hold that every prayer for favour in Scripture is answered by a God who has already promised to be gracious to whom He will be gracious.
